headline: Separate access checks from message review
subtext: Sign-in controls sit outside the inbox so recipients can handle routine upkeep without interrupting sensitive intake.
image_alt_text: A Hush Line daily social graphic showing the desktop Authentication settings page. The screen places account access controls in a separate settings area, away from the inbox where recipients review sensitive messages.

social.bluesky:
Keep account upkeep out of the inbox.

Hush Line separates sign-in controls from message review so recipients and staff can check access details without interrupting sensitive intake.

Learn more at https://hushline.app.
social.linkedin:
Sensitive intake work is easier to manage when account upkeep is not mixed into the inbox.

Hush Line keeps sign-in controls in their own account area, separate from message review. For journalists, lawyers, educators, organizers, and other recipients, that design keeps routine access checks from interrupting the work of reading and triaging disclosures.

Learn more at https://hushline.app.

rationale: This uses the required design_principle format for a recipient-shared screenshot. The angle focuses on separation between access upkeep and sensitive message review, which is distinct from the recent archive post about username, password, and 2FA controls.
copy_brief: Write for recipients and staff using Hush Line day to day, not for platform admins.

editorial_intent.reader_need: Help a recipient or staff member improve a repeatable sensitive-intake workflow.
